title: Sam Parr on cold email, copy work and long-form copy: AIDA, 50 follow-ups, picking businesses
summary: Sam Parr explains how copy work trained his writing, why long-form copy and simple stories convert, and how he writes cold emails with attention, interest, desire, action plus heavy follow-up. He also covers going viral by angering a segment, and hiring by reading people's writing.

principles.text: Write cold emails with AIDA: attention, interest, desire, action, ending on one very specific ask.
principles.quote: the best way to write a cold email is to use this thing called ADA. It's it means attention, interest, desire, action.

principles.text: Follow-ups are the key to cold email; persistence reaches almost anyone.
principles.quote: you're like 50 cold emails away from like everyone on Earth. Like one initial email and 49 follow-ups. Like the follow-up is key.

principles.text: Make follow-ups useful: send event updates and social proof, not nagging.
principles.quote: I would just update them on like the current event of how things were going.

principles.text: Long-form copy converts best because it answers every objection and stories make people feel.
principles.quote: you want to overcome every objection a buyer has. So you need to give them lots of information

principles.text: To go viral, deliberately anger a certain group; make some people love you and others mad.
principles.quote: If you want to go viral with content, the goal should be to piss off a certain type of person.

principles.text: Learn writing by copying great work word for word to absorb rhythm and patterns.
principles.quote: So you just copy word for word writing that you love
